newsitem.title: USA: U.S. sending humanitarian aid team to Zaire.
newsitem.headline: U.S. sending humanitarian aid team to Zaire.

text.p: The United States said on Thursday it may expand humanitarian assistance to Zaire and is sending a team of experts to the central African country to assess the situation.

After talks on Thursday between U.S. officials and the deputy U.N. high commissioner for refugees, Washington "stands prepared ... to expand our humanitarian assistance, if that is required ... ," said U.S. State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns.
"We're sending a USAID (Agency for International Development) disaster ... response team ... to the Great Lakes region," Burns said.

He said the team would leave in the next couple of days and be focused on eastern Zaire, where rebels were reported on Thursday to be advancing on several fronts, including the economically vital mineral provinces of Shaba and Kasai.
Burns insisted the team was a "humanitarian team, not a military team" making preparations for some kind of U.S. military involvement in Zaire.
"I really do want to lead you away from this impression that somehow we're not telling you that we're right on the verge of a military force. I don't think we are," he said.
But he acknowledged "we haven't closed the door" on the multi-national force proposal advanced by France and the United Nations.
"We've agreed to continue to discuss it in the United Nations, but we believe that the current Operation Cease Fire, plus the UN lead on humanitarian supply, is the best way to proceed," he said.

Officials told Reuters on Wednesday that Secretary of State Madeleine Albright, unhappy with options offered her regarding Zaire, directed U.S. experts to rethink plans to help resolve the central African crisis.
On Thursday Burns told reporters: "She has asked our Africa experts to be very thorough in examining all possible options whereby the United States might be helpful."
Officials said this does not necessarily mean the United States will reverse its opposition to a U.N.-French proposal for a multi-national force to intervene in Zaire.
But the issue remains under discussion by the adminstration and with allies, the officials said.
Burns said the situation in Zaire had not improved. "We still don't have a ceasefire (between the government and the rebels) and still don't have an adequate relief operation underway," he said.
